source.licence: None stated: neither GitHub repo has a LICENSE file (GitHub API license=null) and the zip contains no licence or README. Underlying question sources: NQ (CC BY-SA 3.0), TriviaQA (Apache-2.0), WebQuestions (CC BY 4.0), True-False dataset of Azaria & Mitchell (no licence found); responses generated by Llama2-7B (Llama 2 Community License). Because the PiNose release grants no redistribution right, test rows are NOT copied into data/frozen; only an ID + row SHA-256 manifest is frozen and items are rebuilt from data/raw.

public/PiNoseBootstrapData/train_data.cs.note: PiNose pseudo-labelled training triplets; not used

source.response_generator: QA sets: responses generated by Llama2-7B; 'The factuality label for each response is annotated by human annotators through comparing with the original ground-truth of each question' (Section 4.1.1, p. 12352). True-False: statements and labels from the True-False benchmark of Azaria & Mitchell (2023), 'statements generated by LLMs along with corresponding factuality labels examined by humans' (same section); they are not Llama2-7B responses.

frozen.builder: scripts/prepare_pinose.py (downloads + verifies zip, writes manifests; deterministic)
frozen.form: ID + SHA-256 manifest only (no licence); gauntlet.tasks.pinose.items() rebuilds from data/raw and verifies every row hash
frozen.row_hash: sha256 of json.dumps(csv_row_as_released, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':')) in UTF-8; csv_row = csv.DictReader dict of raw strings
frozen.ids: <prefix>-NNNN, NNNN = 0-based data-row index in file order; prefixes tf, nq, triviaqa, webq
frozen.sent_to_jev: QA: {question, response}; True-False: {statement}. The QA reference answer column is never sent (it reveals the label).

test_n_resolution: Exactly 1,000 rows in each of the four released test CSVs. %True matches paper Table 1 (p. 12352) exactly: True-False 405/1000 = 40.5, NQ 466 = 46.6, TriviaQA 495 = 49.5, WebQ 583 = 58.3. The CSVs are row-for-row identical (text and labels) to the released *_feature.parquet files the probe was evaluated on, except TriviaQA row 551 whose empty response is NaN in the parquet (the probe's prompt contained the literal string 'nan').

english_verification.metadata: NQ, TriviaQA and WebQuestions are English QA datasets; True-False (Azaria & Mitchell) is English; responses were generated in English by Llama2-7B.
english_verification.method: langid 1.1.6 (all languages) on every test statement and on every question+response concatenation, plus a census of every non-ASCII character; all flagged rows inspected.
english_verification.result: langid flagged 3 NQ, 0 TriviaQA, 6 WebQ and 18 True-False rows; all are English sentences with foreign proper names (e.g. tf-0077, tf-0941, nq-0786, webq-0951). Non-ASCII characters are Latin diacritics, typographic quotes/dashes, currency and degree signs, one Greek alpha, and one English WebQ response quoting a Chinese term in CJK characters (webq-0501). No non-English or code-mixed rows; no rows dropped.

data_checks.empty_fields: TriviaQA row 551 (id triviaqa-0551): empty response, gold False; kept as released (sent as an empty string)
data_checks.true_false_duplicates: 2 exact duplicate rows (tf-0450 = tf-0818, label 0; tf-0953 = tf-0978, label 1) and 1 conflicting pair (same statement: tf-0053 gold True, tf-0929 gold False); kept as released

deviations: Accuracy threshold fixed a priori at P(true) > 0.5. The paper instead selects the threshold that 'yields the highest accuracy among 100 validation instances partitioned from the test sets' (Section 4.1.4, p. 12353); those 100 instances are not identified in the release, and tuning on test labels is barred here. Jev's ACC is therefore not tuned like the paper's; AUC is threshold-free and directly comparable.
Test rows not redistributed (no licence); frozen ID + SHA-256 manifests instead.
Rows kept verbatim, including one empty TriviaQA response and the True-False duplicates/label conflict.
